title: [Audit follow-up] Approve and correct blocking texture closure policy
body:
Part of the October2026 audit; discovered while implementing#201. Required follow-up from Claude scope pin6092909004: https://github.com/yigini/soilfer-lims/issues/201#issuecomment-6092909004.

The existing blocking `TEXTURE_CLOSURE` gate in `server/controllers/validationController.js:95-109` reparses result text, ignores units, and calls `calculateUsdaTexture` without a tolerance. `server/utils/soilCalculations.js:20,67-87` therefore rejects closure errors above1e-4, although the warning claims±2. At the audited main7ea12c66,40+40+19 is blocked; explicitly passing tolerance2 accepts it. This was verified with the actual pure helper.

#201 preserves that gate byte-for-byte. Its new advisory texture panel uses `crossCheck.textureClosureTolerancePct` and the author-pinned percent-only stored-numeric inputs, so an advisory PASS and a blocking gate refusal may coexist. Both must be disclosed; neither is reconciled by silently weakening the gate.

Before implementing this follow-up, YY must personally sign off the blocking tolerance and applicable analytical policy. Claude explicitly requires that sign-off; the #201 default2 does not authorise changing this gate. Pin the source/units/basis/censoring/ambiguity handling and intended before/after behaviour. All lab policy must use policyService; no hard-coded lab limits or automatic conversions.

Acceptance after that policy is approved:
- Test the approved tolerance boundaries, the40+40+19 example, stored numeric authority versus raw text, percent versus non-percent inputs, missing/censored/non-numeric/ambiguous values, and lab isolation.
- Preserve analytical/QC/audit evidence and existing workflow/tenant/permission guards. Any changed blocking behaviour must be explicit and approved; do not remove tests to force green.
- Run the full server suite and client build/lint, then obtain Claude's exact current-head audit pass and green CI before merge/deploy.

Depends on#201 being merged for integration with its existing advisory panel/evidence. This issue does not authorise a scientific policy value or any production change.
